newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WOODS REGISTERS HISTORIC MASTERS WIN BY RECORD 12 SHOTS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS REGISTERS HISTORIC MASTERS WIN BY RECORD 12 SHOTS.

text.p: Tiger Woods rewrote the record book at Augusta National golf course Sunday, claiming an historic Masters title with a spectacular 12-stroke victory.

Playing with an assurance and maturity astonishing for his age, the 21-year-old Woods became the youngest Masters champion ever and the first black player to win a major golf championship with a performance like none Augusta National had ever seen.

Woods fired a final-round 69 and beat Tom Kite by a dozen strokes to shatter Jack Nicklaus's record for widest victory margin (nine in 1965). He also eclipsed the tournament record total shared by Nicklaus (271 in 1965) and Raymond Floyd (1976) by one stroke.
After sinking his par-putt at 18, Woods celebrated his victory with his familiar fist-pumping gesture of joy to wild cheers from the jam-packed galleries.

Off the green he stopped for some quiet moments with his parents. Woods wiped away a tear after a long hug with his father Earl, who six weeks ago had heart bypass surgery, and then bent to kiss his Thai-born mother Kultida.
"It was an amazing week for me," said Woods, who won $486,000. "It's awesome."
Nick Faldo, three-time winner of the Masters, presented Woods with the green jacket.
"Tiger, that was a phenomenal performance," said the Briton. "And welcome to the green jacket club."
Woods, the three-time U.S. Amateur champion and three-time junior amateur winner, lived up to every outsized expectation the golf world had held for him.

"Tiger is out there playing another game," said Nicklaus, who added another Masters record himself Sunday by playing in his 147th round at Augusta National to surpass Sam Snead by one. "He's playing a golf course he'll own for a long time."
The 57-year-old Nicklaus, a six-time champion, said: "It's not my time anymore. It's his."
